speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand the cause of this bleeding, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the combination of mucous membrane bleeding (gums) and petechiae on the distal extremities in a 4-year-old, we need to check your platelet count immediately. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Platelets. REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu Syndrome).

The normal platelet count and smear rule out thrombocytopenic causes, so the mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae are likely due to vascular malformations or a coagulation factor deficiency. Have you noticed any recurrent nosebleeds in your family, or any visible red spots on your lips or tongue?
